What is wrong with the current one: it is a smooth symmetrical teardrop with a dot in it. A soul is none of those things — it is irregular and trailing — and a symmetrical drop reads as water, or as a generic flame from an icon set. It also belongs to no family: the edit link is now a carved rune and the world control is a sun and moon, and the teardrop rhymes with neither.

Each candidate below sits in the real HUD at 17px, in both worlds.

A — The sigil

Weibo’s Home

Weibo’s Home
PostsAbout

A. The sigil. The site's own carved mark — a stem, a lozenge, a foot. It puts the identity in the same family as the edit rune, so the theme reads as having one vocabulary rather than a collection of icons. Straight strokes hold at any size. The risk is that it is now two runes on one page and they must not be confusable, which is why this one is centred and closed where the edit mark is asymmetric and open.

B — The wisp

Weibo’s Home
PostsAbout
Weibo’s Home
PostsAbout

B. The wisp. The honest soul: asymmetric, leaning, with the body curling one way and a loose spark thrown off the other. Nothing about it is mirrored, which is the whole difference from the teardrop. It is the most atmospheric and the most fragile — irregular curves are exactly what the pixel grid punishes at 17px, so it wants watching on a low-DPI screen.

C — The broken ring

Weibo’s Home
PostsAbout
Weibo’s Home
PostsAbout

C. The broken ring. A soul held in a ring that does not close — the circle is the vessel, the gap is what has gone out of it, the core is what is left. It is the most legible of the four by a distance, because a circle and a dot survive any size or screen, and it rhymes with the world control's disc without repeating it. It is also the most abstract: nothing about it says soul until you are told.

D — No mark

Weibo’s Home

Weibo’s Home

D. No mark. Worth seeing before choosing, because it is what the spec already says: §1 "almost nothing on screen explains itself", §8 "no logo lockup". The name set in Cinzel small caps is the mark. This also returns a gold to the budget — with no mark, the hollowed world spends none at all in the header. The cost is that the site loses the one thing a reader could recognise at a glance in a tab or a bookmark.
